segments.text: Hey everyone, welcome to your daily Robotics news digest for November 19th, 2026.
We've got updates on AI advancements, robotic automation demos, and exciting new robot introductions.
From Robotics & Automation News, "Pudu Robotics rides the tidal wave of China’s AI revolution".
This report details the growth and operational strategy of Pudu Robotics, which has achieved billion-dollar status through the development of commercial service and industrial robots.
The company's success stems from the "One Brain, Multiple Embodiments" strategy, enabling robots to utilize shared artificial intelligence and software foundations.
Pudu Robotics is currently expanding globally, maintaining operations in more than eighty-five countries and having shipped over one hundred thirty thousand robots internationally.
A substantial portion of the company's revenue derives from commercial cleaning robots, which constitute more than seventy percent of the reported twenty twenty five revenue.
Intense competition among Chinese robotics firms is currently reshaping the global industrial landscape.
This trend indicates continued rapid integration of advanced AI into physical automation systems.
From Humanoid.guide, Motion demonstrates Galbot S1 palletizing at Slush summit.
This report details a presentation showcasing the Galbot S1 palletizing robot and the MotionOS software platform.
The demonstration occurred at the Industrial Renaissance Summit in Helsinki on November 19, 2026.
The Galbot S1 robot has a mass of three hundred twenty kilograms and is capable of handling a fifty kilogram payload, employing lidar technology to adjust speed when operating near personnel.
Additionally, Motion unveiled MotionOS, a software platform developed using Google Cloud and Gemini, designed for task qualification, training, and remote support for the robotic systems.
The company operates on a leasing model, serving sectors including food and beverage, heavy industry, and warehouse logistics, highlighting the role of robotics in mitigating labor shortages.
This development indicates continued advancement in the application of sophisticated AI systems within industrial automation.
From Humanoid.guide, welcome to Rho alpha.
This segment reports on the announcement of Microsoft Research's first robotics foundation model, Rho alpha, and its current development status.
The model resides in the software layer of robotics and is derived from Microsoft’s Phi family of AI models.
The Humanoid.Guide Brain Score for Rho alpha is five out of ten, signifying it is an emerging research offering with early access availability.
Access to the model is provided through early access programs on Microsoft Foundry for structured evaluation of its capabilities.
Development of Rho alpha stems from the research lineage and current stage of development rather than specific physical robot specifications.
This introduction of a foundation model into robotics research signals further advancement in AI-driven physical systems.
Industry attention is directed toward ongoing evaluation and subsequent development milestones.
From Humanoid.guide, Foundation unveils Phantom MKII humanoid for industry and defense.
This report details the release of a second-generation humanoid robot designed for heavy industry and defense applications.

Foundation Future Industries has released the Phantom MKII humanoid, which features a Cortex II control system and possesses the capability to navigate adverse weather while carrying two hundred pounds.
This platform is intended for deployment on construction sites and within factories.
The company is exploring the possibility of arming these robots should the United States military request it, based on the rationale that armed ground robots could decrease reliance on drones.
This development follows earlier disputed reports concerning the military potential of previous Phantom models.
The founder of the company clarified that earlier discussions were limited to exploration rather than direct military supply negotiations.
The launch signals an expansion of humanoid robotics into operational industrial and defense sectors.
From The Robot Report, Humyn Labs raises forty-seven million dollars in Series A funding to collect real-world data for robotics.
The company partners with various AI labs and robotics companies to enhance the deployment of robots in practical environments.
Data collection is accomplished through proprietary capture devices that gather information across vision, sound, touch, and motion in more than twenty countries.
This collected data is subsequently processed into labeled, training-ready datasets suitable for residential, commercial, and industrial applications.
The funding is allocated to support necessary infrastructure, hardware development, and on-the-ground presence to accelerate deployment readiness for robotic systems.
This development signifies a focus on creating comprehensive, real-world data essential for advancing practical robotics deployment across various sectors.
From The Robot Report, "From Commercial Scale to Embodied Intelligence: The Next Challenge for Robotics"
reports on the need for greater robotic capability to translate into consistent, scalable, and reliable performance in real-world commercial environments.

Pudu Robotics addresses this challenge by pursuing embodied intelligence through a One Brain, Multiple Embodiments strategy utilizing PuduFM and PuduAgent to establish a shared foundation for extending artificial intelligence capabilities across diverse robot forms.
This approach allows for the expansion of the company's portfolio from commercial settings into residential and outdoor applications, including lawn care robots.
The core objective involves making intelligence reliably operational within the physical world to generate tangible value.
The industry should monitor developments in creating reliable physical interaction for advanced artificial intelligence systems.
From TechCrunch - Robotics, "How Toyota is betting on a future beyond cars".
This report details how Toyota is investing in emerging technologies outside the automotive sector, specifically robotics, physical artificial intelligence, energy, and aerospace.

Through its venture arm, Woven Capital, the automaker invests in startups that are shaping future technology, leveraging industrial expertise to provide portfolio companies with an advantage in manufacturing and supply chain technology.
The strategy explores the evolving venture capital landscape and future opportunities within autonomous fleet infrastructure.
Toyota is pursuing this approach to secure a future extending beyond traditional automotive manufacturing.
This signals a growing focus on applying deep industrial knowledge to advance broader technological innovation across various sectors.
From Robotics & Automation News, factories already using robots more optimistic about automation, finds RobCo study.

This report details a study indicating that businesses already employing robotics demonstrate significantly greater confidence in automating remaining manual processes compared to those in less-automated sectors.
The research involved surveying businesses regarding their awareness of robotics advancements and their optimism concerning the impact of automation on the workforce.
Highly-automated businesses reported greater awareness of robotics advancements and expressed more optimism regarding the workforce impact of automation.
These leading firms also indicated superior integration and adaptability capabilities when compared to less-automated counterparts.

Furthermore, the study revealed that highly-automated entities were more positive about the future consequences of automation on their organizations and industries, with experience correlating to greater optimism regarding job creation through automation.
This data suggests that current implementation of robotics fosters a more positive outlook for technological adoption across industrial sectors.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, PHD Hand!".
This report details the development of a printable humanoid dexterous hand prototype and its key finding is the creation of an accessible mechanical design.

Researchers at the New Jersey Institute of Technology developed a humanoid dexterous hand prototype using an affordable, printable mechanical design incorporating five fingers with linkages and flexible hinges.
The mechanism is driven by miniature servo motors without gear trains and is constructed primarily from materials such as PETG and TPU.
The prototype measures two hundred millimeters and weighs zero point five kilograms, achieving a Humanoid Guide score of four out of ten.
The project intends to promote accessible fabrication by releasing the design files for educational and community use.
This development suggests a step forward in accessible fabrication methods for advanced robotic components.
Further research into similar open-source designs is anticipated within the technology sector.
From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: Fault correlation for ROS 2: one cause, many faults (and what automotive does about it)"
details a method for correlating faults within the Robot Operating System 2 framework, demonstrating that a single underlying issue can cause multiple reported errors in subsequent nodes.
A correlation rule was developed to link a specific lidar connection failure as the root cause to cascading errors such as costmap timeouts and goal rejections.
This process utilized a time window to associate related events and mute the symptoms once the initial fault was identified.
The system suggests using fault history to propose these correlation rules, although human approval remains necessary before implementation.
This research provides a mechanism for improved diagnostic accuracy in complex robotic systems.
The findings indicate a pathway toward more robust fault detection in autonomous systems.
From Robotics & Automation News, Kawasaki Robotics launches F Series S-type controller with integrated safety and cybersecurity.

This report details the introduction of a new controller that combines safety and cybersecurity functionalities with the existing F Series platform, ensuring compliance with evolving European regulations.

Kawasaki Robotics has introduced the F Series Controller S-type, scheduled for availability in November 2026, which seamlessly integrates safety software and cybersecurity features into the established F Series architecture.
This controller incorporates standard CoreCubic-S Lite safety software and includes built-in cybersecurity elements such as user authentication and secure communications.

The S-type is designed to facilitate upgrades from existing F Series B-type controllers and offers optional energy recovery technology, directly addressing requirements set forth by regulations like the EU Machinery Regulation and the Cyber Resilience Act.
This development signals increased integration of security and compliance standards within industrial robotics hardware.
From Robotics & Automation News, Imagry and Endera partner to bring American-made autonomous buses to US transit.
This story details a collaboration aimed at delivering the first Buy America-compliant autonomous buses and shuttles for United States public transit.
The partnership integrates Imagry's Level 4 autonomous driving system with Endera's American-built vehicles.
The objective of this initiative is to enable transit operators across the nation to purchase self-driving options utilizing federal transit funds without requiring a Buy America waiver.
This effort seeks to promote American manufacturing and foster cost-effective autonomous public transport solutions.
The technology development is projected to enhance accessibility and decrease congestion by providing service to underserved regions and increasing public transit efficiency.
This development signals a shift toward integrating domestic manufacturing into advanced autonomous transportation systems.
From The Robot Report, Rockwell Automation acquiring mobile robot maker AGILOX.
This report details the agreement for Rockwell Automation to acquire AGILOX, an Austrian developer of autonomous mobile robots, which is expected to more than double Rockwell's AMR business.
Rockwell Automation will integrate AGILOX into its Intelligent Devices operating segment, bringing expertise in autonomous mobile robots to the company.
The transaction is designed to merge OTTO Motors' North American presence with AGILOX's European customer base.
Furthermore, the acquisition facilitates an exit for global investor Carlyle, which had previously invested in AGILOX.
This strategic move combines hardware and market reach across continents within the automation sector.
The transaction signals continued consolidation within the industrial robotics market.
From Robotics & Automation News, Einride reports 76 percent growth in contracted revenue as autonomous freight operations expand.
This report details the company's significant financial expansion driven by the growth of autonomous freight operations.
Einride achieved $167 million in contracted annual recurring revenue by November 2026.
The growth resulted from the expansion of the customer base and an increase in driverless operating hours under existing customer contracts.
Autonomous freight operations have expanded through projects in Germany and the United States, involving cab-less trucks and agreements established with major manufacturers.
The company is developing autonomous driving systems via collaborations with Nvidia and is training its Saga AI platform.
Einride plans substantial fleet expansion with a target of achieving cash flow breakeven in 2028 and aiming for two billion dollars in annualized revenue by 2030.
This development signals continued progression in the commercial deployment of autonomous freight technology.
From Robotics & Automation News, Hidonix launches the Hido II autonomous rover for indoor mapping, a system demonstrating significant improvements in geospatial data collection efficiency.
Hidonix Industries has released the Hido II autonomous rover designed to automate indoor mapping and geospatial data collection.
The rover incorporates autonomous navigation, advanced sensing capabilities, and a modular robotic arm for collecting geomagnetic and spatial data.
Testing confirmed the rover’s ability to navigate complex indoor environments, including stairs and uneven surfaces, by following predefined routes without continuous manual intervention.

The testing phase indicated that the Hido II system reduced the time required for mapping by fifty percent and achieved positioning errors five times lower than those recorded during manual collection processes.
This achievement is integrated within Hidonix's ION platform for commercial spatial intelligence and robotics.
The deployment of this technology signals advancements in autonomous indoor surveying and data acquisition methods.
From Robotics & Automation News, PIX Moving announces six partnerships to expand autonomous mobility worldwide.
This report details six new strategic collaborations established by PIX Moving to advance autonomous mobility globally through localized service implementation.
These collaborations involve partners such as One-Board, Comobi, CaiiTech, and a Malaysian-based group, concentrating on autonomous shuttle services and last-mile logistics.
The purpose of these partnerships is to translate autonomous vehicle technology into practical, market-specific services by integrating local engineering and operational expertise into the system.

These initiatives support PIX Moving's framework of an open operating model utilizing modular city robotics platforms, addressing engineering, safety, and workforce development across diverse regions.
This development signals a trend toward geographically adapted autonomous deployment in the mobility sector.
From Robohub, "Soft exosuit makes it easier to stand up".
This report details the development of a soft, lightweight exosuit designed to assist elderly individuals in standing from chairs and improving walking efficiency.
Researchers at the Technical University of Munich engineered the suit using artificial tendons and sensors that are guided by machine learning to provide support at the hip during movement.
Testing demonstrated that participants completed more sit-and-stand cycles in less time and experienced a reduced metabolic cost during walking.
Furthermore, users reported feeling in control of their movements while wearing the assistance, indicating a high degree of perceived autonomy.
The design permits comfortable wear over regular clothing, intending to support independence for older adults and those undergoing rehabilitation.
This advancement signals progress in assistive robotics for improving mobility and supporting independent living.
From MIT News - Robotics, "This featherweight, flying robot carries its own sensors and computers".
This report details the development of a flapping-wing microrobot capable of autonomous sensing and computation.
The robot achieved a lift-to-weight ratio of 1.9, enabling it to carry a two hundred and forty-four-milligram electronics package for sensing and computation.
The system incorporates an inertial measurement unit, an optical flow sensor, and a time-of-flight sensor for rapid position estimation without requiring external motion capture.
A novel sensing algorithm was utilized to calculate the robot's orientation and position swiftly, resulting in positional accuracy comparable to offboard cameras.
This technology demonstrates potential for applications in precision agriculture and industrial surveillance.
Future developments in autonomous micro-robotics are anticipated in this field.
From The Verge - Robots, "Disney’s new Star Wars animatronics interact with guests using AI".
This report details the development of three new Star Wars animatronic prototypes that interact with guests through artificial intelligence.

These prototypes are named Vilo Vele, Kado Bre’a, and Jibu Bre’a and utilize hidden cameras and microphones to capture guest interactions which are then processed by AI models on Amazon Web Services to guide their real-time responses such as making eye contact.
All movements and dialogue for these creations are prewritten by Disney Imagineers to ensure character accuracy.
These new creations are slated for debut in Las Vegas and potential integration into Disney parks.
The application of AI in creating dynamic character interaction sets a precedent for immersive entertainment technologies.
From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: ROS 2 on macOS: measured topic rates for each RMW, a Fast DDS shared-memory pitfall, and tuned presets"
details the performance measurement of ROS 2 Real-Time Middleware implementations on macOS and presents specific findings regarding transport performance.
Benchmarking of various RMW implementations on macOS revealed significant performance variations dependent on the transport layer utilized.
The investigation examined the performance of Fast DDS, Cyclone DDS with iceoryx, and Zenoh.
The results indicated that Fast DDS's default shared-memory transport on macOS introduced a polling tick delay, resulting in message bursts and elevated latency.
Cyclone DDS with iceoryx demonstrated the highest performance, achieving rates up to 200 kHz with minimal latency.
Zenoh provided a balanced performance profile, particularly when batching was disabled for high rates and shared memory enabled for larger messages.
These measurements guide the selection of appropriate RMWs based on message size and required throughput for system design.
Future development should focus on utilizing these transport-specific optimizations for high-performance ROS deployments.
From NVIDIA Developer Blog, "Build Training-Ready Physical AI Datasets with Two Prompts in NVIDIA Cosmos".

This report details the use of the NVIDIA Cosmos platform to accelerate the creation of physical AI training datasets, achieving up to sixty times faster and forty-five times cheaper assembly compared to traditional methods.
The NVIDIA Cosmos platform incorporates the Data Factory to facilitate data curation, processing, and synthetic data generation through coding agents and blueprints to orchestrate workflows.

This system addresses five use cases including generating autonomous vehicle scenarios, augmenting images and videos, creating rare event videos, and generating defect images by leveraging core agent skills such as Auto Labeling and Augmentation to convert data gaps into generation jobs.
This methodology demonstrates a significant reduction in the resources required for complex dataset assembly.
The development signals a shift toward automated, scalable data generation for physical AI training applications.
And that's all the circuits for today!
Hope you enjoyed diving into Pudu Robotics and the AI tide.
Until tomorrow, keep those algorithms humming.
